3fp6pm:412: The FDU model marks a fundamental rethink by IBM of the nature of enterprise AI delivery. The traditional model follows a linear headcount-expansion logic—scaling a project means deploying more consultant manpower, with delivery quality highly dependent on individual capability and obvious scalability bottlenecks. Through the combination of small senior-level teams + AI agents, FDU attempts to break this linear relationship: a six-person team accomplishes what traditionally required teams of dozens. The core difference is that AI handles repetitive execution work such as coding, evaluation, testing, and documentation, while humans focus on judgment-heavy decisions and client alignment. The economic implications of this shift are worth examining: the traditional consulting billing model is based on "person-days"—value creation = headcount × time × rate. FDU seeks to shift the anchor of value creation to "platform intelligence × operational continuity," which means both billing logic and profit pool distribution are likely to undergo structural changes. IBM is no longer just selling people's time; it is selling the capability of an end-to-end delivery system.
